responsibilities.label: Maintenance
responsibilities.explanation: Keeping database software and its servers updated. The provider handles routine work, but you may still need to choose maintenance times or plan upgrades to a new major software version.

responsibilities.label: Connection pooling
responsibilities.explanation: Connection pooling means reusing database connections instead of opening a new one for every request. You usually configure this in your app or use a connection-sharing tool. D1 connects directly to Worker code. DynamoDB and Firestore Standard use request-based connections rather than traditional database pools. Supavisor and PgBouncer are connection-pooling tools.
values: Configure the app or RDS Proxy
Configure pooling in the database library
Configure the app or a supported pooling tool
Configure the app or RDS Proxy

responsibilities.label: Simultaneous requests
responsibilities.explanation: Handling requests that arrive at the same time. A provider-run database still limits connections, simultaneous work and processing speed. D1 processes queries one at a time within each database copy.
values: Several at once, within capacity limits
One query at a time per database copy

responsibilities.label: Backups and recovery history
responsibilities.explanation: Backups keep copies that can be restored. Point-in-time recovery lets you return data to a chosen moment within the saved history. Available features, history length and charges depend on the plan. Having backups does not prove that recovery will be fast or complete enough for your app.

responsibilities.explanation: Recovering data from a backup or saved history. You choose the recovery point, start the restore and check the result. Some products create a new database server or group of servers, so you may need to reconnect your app after recovery.

responsibilities.explanation: Changing how much processing power the database has. Manual includes enabling automatic capacity changes and setting their limits: after setup, those changes can happen automatically. D1 does not offer a database server-size setting.

responsibilities.label: Storage growth
responsibilities.explanation: Increasing the room available for data. Some products grow storage automatically within limits; others require settings or a plan change. At a database's size limit you may need to split data across several databases.

responsibilities.label: Read-only copies
responsibilities.explanation: Read replicas are database copies used to answer read requests. You may need to create them and direct reads to them. Copies can be behind the latest writes, so choose how up-to-date reads must be. A read-only copy is not a historical backup.

responsibilities.label: Staying online after failures
responsibilities.explanation: High availability means reducing downtime when machines fail. Failover means switching to a working replacement. Recovery on one site, across separate sites and across regions offers different protection. Check the service and plan: Auto does not mean there can be no downtime.

responsibilities.label: Monitoring and alerts
responsibilities.explanation: Watching database health, usage and failures. Providers supply measurements, but you choose which values need attention, who receives alerts and how to respond. Collecting measurements alone does not notify anyone or fix a problem.
